post.title: SPACE: Firecracker Sandbox Platform
post.hook: A sandbox platform whose benchmarks check that memory survives suspend and restore.
post.summary: SPACE is a Rust sandbox platform that runs code in isolated Firecracker microVMs behind an HTTP API. The repo has docs, a Kind dev setup, typed smoke scenarios and a set of worker-node benchmarks.
post.writeup:
## What it is

SPACE (Sandboxed Platform for Agentic Code Execution) runs code in isolated Firecracker microVMs. Applications use an HTTP API to create Linux environments from templates, run commands, collect output and manage sandbox lifecycles. The repo holds 3399 files, 79.4% of them Rust, with Python, Shell and Go around it.

## Why it exists

An agent, a user workspace or a code-running job needs its own execution environment. The application decides what to run and what to keep. SPACE manages the sandbox, its processes and the connection that carries command output.

## How it works

A template supplies the starting environment. A sandbox is an instance with its own VM and writable filesystem. Lifecycle changes are asynchronous: the API returns an operation ID to poll. Command output uses a separate data-plane connection with a session-scoped attachment token. Sandboxes can be kept, paused, suspended and woken. An E2B Compatibility Wrapper lets the tested E2B Python SDK talk to it.

## What the repo shows

- Database migrations are immutable once applied, with a checksum registry for reviewed equivalent edits.
- Smoke tests are typed scenarios (ecw, network_policy, native, local) run across four Kind CI shards.
- Benchmarks on one worker node cover concurrent lifecycle ops, create latency under density, and balloon suspend/restore. The balloon benchmark runs build, alloc-free, file-heavy and idle profiles, checksums guest memory and rootfs after each restore, and gates variants on at least 10% and 64 MiB smaller snapshot memory.
- Git history shows 50 commits from 7 authors on 2026-10-21 and 2026-10-22.

## Open questions

The benchmark docs describe the method but the material has no result numbers, so the snapshot-size gains from balloon variants are unmeasured here.
